bank.keyText: A plant can take from a network without giving back
choiceTexts: Chlorophyll turns out to be unnecessary for the majority of land plants
Fungi favour hosts that have given up photosynthesis
Trees raise their sugar output when a network drains carbon from them
A plant can take from a network without giving back
Most plants in a forest obtain their carbon from other plants

difficulty.from: question type (inference from an example); the RC bank has no difficulty field

answer.text: A plant can take from a network without giving back
answer.line: Ghost pipe makes no sugar and lives on carbon from fungi joined to trees. Paragraph 15 adds: these plants return nothing.

steps: Find the example: paragraph 15. The author says it proves two things: "It also cuts the other way."
First, carbon can cross a fungus into another plant. Second, these plants return nothing.
Match the second point. A plant that takes and never gives back is what the example most strongly supports.

choices.text: Chlorophyll turns out to be unnecessary for the majority of land plants
choices.note: Ghost pipe and a number of orchids are one small group, sentence 2. Nothing stretches that to most land plants.

choices.text: Fungi favour hosts that have given up photosynthesis
choices.note: No fungal preference is described. The same fungi are attached to photosynthetic trees at the same time.

choices.text: Trees raise their sugar output when a network drains carbon from them
choices.note: Trees raising their output never comes up. This invents a response the passage does not describe.

choices.text: A plant can take from a network without giving back
Most plants in a forest obtain their carbon from other plants
choices.note: One unusual group cannot carry a claim about most plants. The forest trees in the passage make their own sugar.

lockIt: Examples in a passage: ask what the author says the example shows, and how far it reaches.

spans.quote: Ghost pipe and a number of orchids carry no usable chlorophyll and make no sugar at all
spans.choice: Chlorophyll turns out to be unnecessary for the majority of land plants
spans.note: one named group, not most plants

spans.quote: The route says nothing about generosity at either end
spans.note: the half that cuts the other way
